edits.current: Not an employee where no employment contract exists: directors' fees are not employment income and are not produced by payroll. The withholding on them is declared by the employer's accounts-payable or tax function - in the natural-person fees casillas (79 / 95, or 77 / 93 where the fee is withheld under the ET art. 383 table, art. 383 para. 2) for a resident director and under sheet-2 concept 25 (Honorarios de directores) for a non-resident director - never as payroll employment income. A director holding an employment contract is reported as an ordinary employee (see 'Executive director / statutory legal representative holding an employment contract').

edits.current: Casillas 29-54 (legal persons) and 79-108 (natural persons). Not produced by payroll: populated by the employer's accounts-payable or tax function. Form 350 aggregates every withholding the employer makes; payroll contributes only casillas 77 / 93, casillas 78 / 94 where the employer pays pensions itself, the sheet-2 rows for non-resident employees and casilla 129 where a prior over-withholding is reversed.

edits.current: A period with no operation subject to withholding is not filed: ET art. 606 para. 2 makes the return non-obligatory for such a period (Population Rules, 'Nil period'). The electronic payroll and PILA have no equivalent exemption, so a month with employees but no withholding still produces those two filings and no Form 350.
